news.title: European FAs reveal U20 Women's World Cup squads despite UEFA boycott
news.lede: UEFA announced it would boycott all FIFA tournaments after FIFA president Gianni Infantino announced plans to sell part of the FIFA World Cup through FIFA Forward Enterprise, a $20 billion subsidiary that would sell 20 per cent of the tournament to private investors. The 55 UEFA members unanimously voted to boycott FIFA tournaments as long as the sell-off plans were on the table, and UEFA president Aleksander Ceferin said they would keep up the boycott after FIFA and Infantino withdrew the plans, saying conditions had not been met. "First, the proposals to sell off the major competitions had to be withdrawn, and secondly, assurances have to be made that such attempts to disfigure the game in this way will never be made again. These conditions have not been met," Ceferin said in a statement.

news.title: FIFA slaps Argentina with hefty fine, punishments after World Cup final chaos
news.lede: FIFA has punished the Argentine Football Association (AFA) and several members of Argentina's squad and coaching staff for disciplinary violations arising from the 2026 World Cup, including the confrontation that followed the final on July 19. The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has been ordered to pay $321,000 in fines after FIFA found multiple disciplinary violations during the World Cup. Among the incidents cited was a banner displayed by some Argentina players after their semi-final victory over England. The message read “Las Malvinas Son Argentinas”, translating to “The Falklands are Argentine”.

news.title: The Argentine Football Federation was fined 321,000 dollars for the incidents in the World Cup final / Paredes, suspended for 10 matches
news.lede: Leandro Paredes, the midfielder of the Argentine national team, has been suspended for 10 matches and fined $90,000 by FIFA, following a violent altercation at the end of the match between Argentina and Spain, held at the New York New Jersey stadium. The incident occurred after the final whistle, when Paredes slammed Spanish international Gavi to the ground, escalating tensions between the two teams. FIFA has also decided to sanction other members of the Argentine delegation, including Nahuel Molina, who received a seven-match suspension and a similar fine, and Thiago Almada, who will miss one match and will pay $30,000. Roberto Ayala, an official in the Argentine staff, has been suspended for three matches.

news.title: 2026 World Cup : FIFA hands Leandro Paredes a 10-match ban
news.lede: FIFA has announced disciplinary sanctions against several Argentina players and staff members following the clashes that erupted after the 2026 World Cup final against Spain. Leandro Paredes received the heaviest punishment, with FIFA handing the Boca Juniors midfielder a 10-match suspension and a €77,000 fine. Paredes played a central role in the post-match confrontation and notably attacked Barcelona midfielder Gavi after Argentina’s 1-0 defeat in extra time. Nahuel Molina also received a heavy punishment, with a seven-match suspension and a €77,000 fine.

news.title: FIFA bans Leandro Paredes for 10 matches over World Cup final scuffle
news.lede: Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes has been handed a 10-match ban by FIFA following a scuffle with Spain players moments after the World Cup final. Paredes received the longest suspension among three Argentina players punished for the incident. The sanctions were announced by FIFA on Friday.Argentina defender Nahuel Molina has been suspended for seven matches, while Thiago Almada has received a one-match ban.The punishments were not limited to Argentina.Spain midfielder Gavi has also been suspended following the incident.

news.title: Paredes banned for 10 games after World Cup final fracas, Argentina fined
news.lede: Argentina’s Leandro Paredes received a 10-match suspension, while teammate Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games. Argentina’s Leandro Paredes received a 10-match suspension for his part in a brawl after his team lost to Spain in the World Cup Final while teammate Nahuel Molina was suspended for seven games, FIFA announced on Aug 21. A brief scuffle erupted at the final whistle when Argentina midfielder Paredes shoved Spain’s Gavi to the ground as the European champions’ substitutes rushed onto the pitch to celebrate. Paredes faced three assault counts while Molina faced two.

news.title: Argentina fined $321,000 over Falklands World Cup protest - as Paredes faces 10 match ban
news.lede: Fifa's Disciplinary Committee announced on Friday that the Argentinian Football Association (AFA) has been fined a total of $321,000 for several breaches of its code. Argentina has been fined $321,000 by Fifa over its Falklands World Cup protest that saw several players and coaching staff unfurl a banner following their triumph over England. Argentinian defensive midfielder Leandro Paredes, 32, now faces a 10-match ban as a result of his involvement in the stunt, which breached article 13 of Fifa's sporting code, the footballing body confirmed. Fifa's Disciplinary Committee also announced on Friday that the Argentinian Football Association (AFA) has been fined a total of $321,000 for several breaches of its code relating to both player and fan behaviour.
